motivation: Exact-point returns after one-year Thalassia loss are more fragile than uninterrupted occupancy. Test whether pre-loss focal persistence history identifies which returned points remain stable one year later.

primary_population.four_year_sequence: same stable point observed in t,t+1,t+2,t+3; t>=2016; t+3<=2025
primary_population.recovered_pattern: Thalassia present at t, absent at t+1, present at t+2
primary_population.pre_loss_run_length: immediately consecutive consensus years ending at t with Thalassia present

primary_hypothesis.statement: Among exact-point Thalassia returns, longer-than-usual pre-loss focal persistence history predicts lower probability of re-loss in the next year.
primary_hypothesis.primary_predictor: pre_loss_run_length centered by stable-node mean among recovered sequences
primary_hypothesis.model: L2 logistic regression for recorded re-loss
primary_hypothesis.support_rule: upper bound of 95% node-bootstrap interval for the centered pre-loss run-length coefficient < 0

secondary: re-loss fraction by integer pre-loss run length where >=5 recovered sequences occur
loss-year vegetation-continuity coefficient in the same model, descriptive only

interpretation.supported: Longer focal persistence history is associated with more stable re-recording after loss, consistent with local legacy contributing to recovery depth as well as return probability.
interpretation.unsupported: Pre-loss focal history predicts reappearance but does not robustly distinguish stable versus fragile returns one year later.

claim_boundary: Post-hoc endpoint derived from an already-opened four-year return-fragility result.
Recorded re-loss is not demographic relapse, mortality, or failed recolonization.
A history effect would not prove rhizome or clonal memory without direct below-ground measurements.
Loss-year vegetation continuity is a state marker, not a causal facilitation treatment.
Do not change the recovered pattern, history definition, node-centering, controls, model, minima, or directional support rule after opening the stability-history result.
